sources.quote: Frankfurt, Harry G., 1969, "Alternate Possibilities and Moral Responsibility", The Journal of Philosophy, 66(23): 829–839.
In an influential 1969 paper, Harry Frankfurt offers examples meant to show that an agent can be morally responsible for an action even if he could not have done otherwise.

claims.text: hoan_canh: Jones, Black can ép Jones nhưng không can thiệp; Jones tự làm

sources.quote: another agent, Black, would like to see Jones perform this action and, if necessary, Black can make Jones perform it by intervening ... Black does not intervene to ensure Jones's action.
Black has the power to interfere with Jones in a way that ensures that Jones does exactly what Black wants him to do.

claims.text: lua_chon b: Nguyên tắc khả năng thay thế (PAP)

sources.quote: PAP: a person is morally responsible for what he has done only if he could have done otherwise.

claims.text: lua_chon a / phan_bien b: Frankfurt cho rằng trách nhiệm không cần khả năng làm khác

sources.quote: Jones could not have done otherwise, yet he seems responsible for his behavior since he does it on his own.

claims.text: phan_bien a: lời đáp của người phản đối (flickers of freedom, tất định)

sources.quote: Incompatibilists replied with the "flickers of freedom" response ... most compatibilists were convinced, most incompatibilists were not.

notes: Ví dụ bỏ phiếu A/B của site là biến thể thường dùng trong tài liệu sau (SEP nêu Jones/Black nói chung); bản gốc Frankfurt 1969 dùng hành động nói chung. Không mở được toàn văn bài 1969; chỉ xác nhận qua SEP. Không có số liệu PhilPapers (so_lieu_khao_sat null, đúng).
